nodes.name: NiFe2-MIL-88 to NiFeP nanorods
nodes.procedure: NiFe2-MIL-88 precursor was first carbonized at 450 °C under air to form NiFe2O4 nanorods. Then the NiFe2O4 nanorods were phosphated at 400 °C under N2 flow with NaH2PO2 as phosphorus source to obtain NiFeP nanorods that remained the size and shape of the original NiFe2-MIL-88 precursor.

unit_operations.name: Carbonization
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: NiFe2-MIL-88 was carbonized at 450 °C under air to prepare NiFe2O4 nanorods

unit_operations.name: Phosphating
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: phosphating the as-prepared NiFe2O4 nanorods at 400 °C under N2 flow with NaH2PO2 as the phosphorus source

nodes.source_text: Wang and coworkers reported a facile strategy to fabricate nickel-iron bimetallic phosphides nanorods from the NiFe2-MIL-88 precursor. Firstly, NiFe2O4 nanorods were prepared by carbonization of NiFe2-MIL-88 at 450 °C under air. Then, NiFeP nanorods were obtained by phosphating the as-prepared NiFe2O4 nanorods at 400 °C under N2 flow with NaH2PO2 as the phosphorus source.

nodes.name: Cu/PTA-MOPF pyrolysis to Cu3P/CNS
nodes.procedure: Cu/PTA-MOPF was fabricated through mixing PTA and Cu(NO3)2 in 1:1 molar ratio where PTA acted as reducing agent and stabilizer, then self-assembled, and finally directly pyrolyzed at 500 °C under Ar atmosphere without additional P sources. During pyrolysis, PTA provided P source to react with Cu to form Cu3P.
nodes.source_text: Zhou and coworkers used... Cu/PTA-MOPF was constructed through the self-assembly of Cu(I) and PTA/PTAH. Then, Cu3P/CNS was prepared via directly pyrolyzing Cu/PTA-MOPF at 500 °C under Ar without additional P sources.

nodes.name: ZIF-67 pyrolysis to Co/N-C then phosphosulfurization
nodes.procedure: ZIF-67 was pyrolyzed into Co/N-C at 600 °C under N2 and subsequent further vacuum phosphosulfurization to prepare CoPS/N-doped carbon nanocomposites.
